summary: Iteration 4 verified the NEW provider-subscription feature (native OpenAI-compatible providers + per-model OpenRouter fallback) plus full regression. Backend: 27 pytest tests (21 pre-existing + 6 new in test_providers.py) — 27 passed / 0 failed. New checks: /api/council exposes providers[] {id,label,configured} + openrouter_configured + any_provider_configured + members carry provider/native_model/routing; POST /api/settings with provider_keys {openai:'sk-test-fake-...'} persists, GET /api/settings & /api/council & POST response NEVER contain the raw key text (verified via full-text substring assertions), routing/native_models persist; routing 'openrouter' with no OR key returns graceful 400 mentioning OpenRouter; routing 'direct' with a fake OpenAI key attempts direct, fails, falls back to OR, and returns graceful 400/502 (no 500); routing 'auto' with no keys returns graceful 400/502. Regression: council roster (5 + scribe), sessions CRUD, message length cap 422 @8001, synth question cap 422 @4001, TTS text cap 422 @8001, STT 415 on non-audio & non-415 on audio/mpeg, CORS, expensive-endpoint rate-limit burst still yields 429, PDF export still returns application/pdf with %PDF magic (>500 bytes), review 'two members must speak' guard. Frontend smoke: home shows amber 'Add subscription or OpenRouter key' when unset; open-settings-btn opens dialog containing provider-key-openai/anthropic/gemini/deepseek/moonshot, openrouter-key-input, route-gpt-auto/direct/openrouter, native-model-gpt, model-id-gpt, persona-gpt, notetaker-model, save-settings-btn — all present. Save works, toast 'Settings saved' shown; reopening shows 'active' badge and '•••• saved — paste to replace' placeholder. Home status line flips to green 'models linked'. Raw key never appears in DOM. Convene → chamber navigates and full dock renders (synthesize-btn, auto-debate-btn, review-btn, conclude-btn, export-btn, mic-btn, send-btn).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py generate() catches HTTPException in the route loop and continues to next route — for pref='direct' with fake key, direct raises ProviderError (Exception) so it falls back to openrouter; but if direct raised HTTPException it would still try openrouter due to `continue`. This is intended behavior (per-model fallback on error) but note that a legitimate downstream 401/403 from provider will be silently retried on OpenRouter. Consider surfacing which route ultimately failed in the error detail for observability.

SettingsDialog auto-fills the OpenRouter model input with the default per-member `mem.model` on every open. If the user has customized a native model but never touched model-id-<id>, the default OpenRouter id is persisted verbatim on Save. Not a bug but means POST /settings will always include 'models' with defaults — mildly inefficient and could accidentally overwrite a server-side override that wasn't returned to the client (currently backend does return s.get('models',{}) so parity is fine).
provider_keys stored as plain strings in the settings doc. Since the backend never returns them, this is only a data-at-rest concern; consider Fernet/KMS encryption for the DB field.

Routing options and provider labels are duplicated between backend PROVIDERS map and frontend ROUTES list — kept in sync manually. Would benefit from an /api/meta endpoint that returns both to avoid drift.
The 'openrouter_configured' field on /api/settings response body is included but 'openrouter_key' or 'provider_keys' fields are correctly OMITTED — assertion passes. Good.
